title: Self-hosted web interface
description: Host browser management and public file landings alongside your own storage API.

sections.title: Separate your web and API origins
paragraphs: The public loft site is documentation and marketing only. Your installation can serve /app for management, /s/<link> for shares, and /r/<token> for file requests.
Set VITE_API to the API origin when building the web interface. Set LOFT_WEB on the API to the origin where you serve those pages.

sections.title: Build for your installation
paragraphs: Leave VITE_MARKETING_ONLY unset for a self-hosted installation. It is enabled only for the public marketing deployment.

sections.title: Serve the static output
paragraphs: Publish apps/web/dist using your own static web server. Configure /app, /app/*, /s/*, and /r/* to fall back to index.html so direct links work.
The repository’s Vercel configuration intentionally redirects /app and omits share/request routes for the public site. Use your own hosting configuration for the self-hosted interface.

sections.title: Connect in your browser
paragraphs: Open /app on your web origin and enter your operator token in settings. That token is stored locally in the browser and is sent to the configured API. It is not a hosted loft login.
When changing VITE_API, rebuild the frontend. Restarting a static server does not update the API origin embedded in its JavaScript.
